intro.en: Aleph. The first letter, the number one, the breath before every word.
intro.src: The first of the three mother letters

lines.en: Look closely: an aleph is drawn from three letters. A yod above, a yod below, and a vav between them.
Yod, vav, yod: 10 + 6 + 10 = 26, the number of God's four-letter Name, hidden inside the first letter.
The upper yod is the waters above, the lower yod the waters below, the vav the sky between them.
lines.src: Genesis 1:7, as the mystics read it

lines.en: Aleph makes no sound of its own. It is the open breath that every vowel rides on.
Aleph was made king over air: the sky in the world, the mild season in the year, the chest in the body.
Some sages taught that at Sinai the people heard only the aleph of Anochi, "I am": a silence holding every word.
Echad, one, begins with aleph. In the Zohar God tells it: my oneness is known only through you.
Turn aleph around and read it backwards: אלף becomes פלא, pele. Wonder.
In the oldest Hebrew script aleph was an ox's head, horns and all: the strength that pulls the plough.
The same three letters spell aluf, master; elef, a thousand; and a'alefcha, I will teach you.
Three mother letters: aleph, mem, shin. Air, water, fire. Aleph is the air between, keeping fire and water in balance.
Aleph is one. Spelled in full, אלף adds to 111: one, ten, a hundred. One at every level.
Every letter asked to begin the world. Aleph alone held back, and was promised the first word at Sinai.

intro.en: Mem. The mother letter of water, the hum of closed lips, the number forty.
intro.src: The second of the three mother letters

lines.en: A song of ascents: from the depths I call to You. The climb begins at the bottom, in the deep water.
As water gives a face back to a face, so one heart answers another.
Mem is forty: forty days of rain, forty days on the mountain, forty years in the desert, forty measures of water in a mikveh.
In the oldest Hebrew script mem was drawn as a line of waves. It is named for water, mayim.
Mem hums with the lips closed, shin hisses, and aleph is the breath that keeps the balance between them.
Ho, all who are thirsty, come to the water. The sages read it: there is no water but Torah.
Mem was made king over water: the earth in the world, the cold season in the year, the belly in the body.
Mem has two forms, open מ and closed ם. The sages said: an open teaching and a hidden one.
Emet, truth: aleph from the start of the letters, mem from the middle, tav from the end. Truth is the seal of God.
Shamayim, the heavens, were made of fire and water mixed together: esh and mayim, shin and mem.

intro.en: Shin. The mother letter of fire, the hiss of the flame, three heads rising from one root.
intro.src: The third of the three mother letters

lines.en: Moses saw a bush burning with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
The soul of a person is the lamp of God. Like a flame, it reaches up.
On the tefillin worn on the head a shin is pressed into the leather on both sides: three heads on one side, four on the other.
Three heads rising from one root: the mystics see in them the three fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Love is as strong as death. Its sparks are sparks of fire, a flame of God.
Shin hisses like a flame, mem hums like water, and aleph is the breath between them.
Shamayim, the heavens, were made of fire and water mixed together: esh and mayim.
Shin was made king over fire: the heavens in the world, the heat in the year, the head in the body.
Man and woman, ish and ishah, share the letters of esh, fire. What keeps it from consuming them is God's Name between them, yod and heh.
Shaddai, the Name written on the outside of every mezuzah, begins with shin.
Shema, Shabbat, shalom: the words at the heart of a Jewish day all begin with shin.
